scenes.label: Meet the team
scenes.title: The familiar profile
scenes.caption: Arjun receives an imaginary message from his project partner’s familiar profile. It asks for a private project folder and a voucher immediately. The picture and nickname match, so Arjun initially assumes his friend must be writing the message.
scenes.dialogue: A profile is an identity claim.

scenes.label: The problem
scenes.title: What is being requested?
scenes.caption: The folder includes other pupils’ work. The voucher would transfer value. A classmate points out that a copied profile or an account controlled by someone else could make the same request. Familiar appearance alone does not identify the sender.

scenes.label: How it works
scenes.title: A narrowing deadline
scenes.caption: The sender says a teacher will be angry if Arjun waits. This adds pressure without supplying evidence. Asking the same account whether it is really his friend would only let whoever controls that account repeat the claim.
scenes.dialogue: A repeated claim is not confirmation.

scenes.label: Your decision
scenes.title: An independent check
scenes.caption: Arjun considers sending the folder, buying the voucher, or contacting his friend through a phone route already known to his family. Choose the plan that checks identity without releasing classmates’ work or spending money while the request remains uncertain.

scenes.label: What changes
scenes.title: The friend answers
scenes.caption: The real friend denies sending it. Arjun stops responding to the suspicious account and tells a trusted teacher. They keep a minimal fictional record and use the platform’s reporting route, without publicly accusing the friend of attempting fraud.

scenes.label: Enter the lab
scenes.title: Another channel appears
scenes.caption: A new message arrives from an unfamiliar number, claiming the old phone is broken. In the lab, explain why that new number cannot verify itself and revise the verification and reporting plan.
